eligibility: Graduates from Sub-Saharan African countries with a bachelor's degree (at least Second Class Upper or equivalent, completed within the last 6 years); this award is tied to the MSc in Water and Environmental Engineering at 2iE.
funding: Funded (tuition and programme support for the normal duration of the Master's, usually up to 2 years)
organization: DAAD / International Institute for Water and Environmental Engineering (2iE)
source: Scholarship aggregators reporting the official DAAD call (verify on the DAAD scholarship database)
summary: DAAD In-Country/In-Region scholarship for the 2027 intake, attached to the MSc in Water and Environmental Engineering at 2iE in Burkina Faso. One of the closest possible field matches — and the DAAD portal closes 12 November 2026, so act immediately and check the host university's own admission deadline too.
title: DAAD In-Country/In-Region Scholarship — MSc Water & Environmental Engineering (2iE)

eligibility: Bachelor's degree in civil or environmental engineering, geosciences, environmental sciences, geography, geology, natural resources or a related field. Partner-country deadline (which covers Nigeria) is 3 January 2027; programme countries close 7 February 2027.
funding: Fully funded — Erasmus Mundus scholarship, €1,400/month for the 2-year programme plus participation costs
location: Netherlands, Germany & Portugal (IHE Delft / TU Dresden / University of Lisbon)
organization: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master — GroundwatCh (IHE Delft, TU Dresden, University of Lisbon)
source: Scholarships.af summary of the Erasmus Mundus programme (verify in the official Erasmus Mundus Catalogue)
summary: Two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Groundwater and Global Change: groundwater hydrology and climate adaptation taught across IHE Delft, TU Dresden and Lisbon. About 15 scholarships are awarded per intake and partner-country applicants compete for the January deadline.
title: GroundwatCh Erasmus Mundus MSc — Groundwater & Global Change

eligibility: Postgraduate students, final-year bachelor's students, or graduates who can start within one year of graduating. Environmental, water-resource or development studies are desirable; English proficiency required.
funding: Stipend provided under UN rules (amount not stated)
source: Opportunities Feed summary of the UNDP vacancy (apply via the UNDP jobs portal)
summary: Six-month, full-time internship with UNDP's Regional International Waters Team: research, databases, analysis, communications and project coordination on international waters. Combine a cover letter (including availability) and CV into a single PDF to apply.
title: UNDP International Waters Internship

eligibility: Bachelor's degree in Agricultural, Irrigation, Civil, Water or Environmental Engineering (or related), at least 4 years of relevant irrigation / hydraulic engineering experience; COREN registration is an advantage.
location: Kano, Nigeria (with travel to project sites)
summary: Water and Irrigation Engineer for a fast-growing agribusiness and climate-smart infrastructure company in Kano: efficient water management and sustainability across irrigation and hydraulic projects in northern Nigeria. Direct field match and Nigerian location, but written for someone with about four years' experience.
title: Water & Irrigation Engineer

eligibility: Bachelor's, Master's or equivalent in a relevant subject (including Water Resources Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Hydrology) obtained within the last two years.
source: Sara Bangla News report of the official RRI notice
summary: Three-month internships for 12 students in two batches (January–March 2027 and April–June 2027) at Bangladesh's River Research Institute, covering river engineering, hydraulics and water resources. Apply using the prescribed form linked in the official notice.
title: River Research Institute Internship

eligibility: Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Engineering or a related discipline, with 3–5 years' experience in sustainability / CSR implementation.
summary: Sustainability Specialist in Lagos covering ESG reporting, environmental compliance (ISO 14001, NESREA), water stewardship, water efficiency and waste/circular-economy initiatives across plants. Environmental rather than pure water engineering, hence a step below the Kano engineering role.
title: Sustainability Specialist

eligibility: Master's degree in Public Health, Water and Sanitation, Environmental Engineering or a related field plus at least 5 years of professional WASH experience. A bachelor's in Civil / Water Resources / Environmental / Sanitary Engineering is an advantage. See listing for the closing date.
funding: Paid job (UN National Officer salary scale — see listing)
source: NGOJobsite summary of the UNICEF vacancy (verify on UNICEF Careers)
summary: WASH Specialist (NO-3) strengthening the evidence base and results orientation of UNICEF Nigeria's WASH programme, including oversight of the DGIS-funded ASWA III project. Kept on the board because it is a flagship Nigerian WASH role and a useful career target — but it is senior (Master's + 5 years), so it scores lower for a student audience.
title: WASH Specialist (NO-3)

eligibility: University degree, or currently pursuing an advanced degree, in engineering, environmental studies, development studies, environmental policy or a related field. Applicants must hold a residence/work permit for Denmark; French is desirable.
location: Copenhagen, Denmark (UNEP — Climate Technology Centre & Network)
source: Career Bridge Africa summary of the UNEP vacancy
summary: Six-month internship starting 7 January 2027 supporting coordination of climate-mitigation technical assistance in Africa. Strong UN brand and relevant environmental content, but it is unpaid and Copenhagen-based with a Danish residence/work-permit requirement — that restriction is why it scores lower for a Nigeria-based student.
title: UNEP CTCN Internship — Mitigation Support
